meta.description: End-to-end pooled and single-cell CRISPR screen analysis from FASTQ to hit genes: library QC, guide counting, six-stage screen QC, method-matched hit calling across MAGeCK/BAGEL2/drugZ/JACKS/Chronos, copy-number and batch correction, and tier-based cross-method consensus, with branches to editing/single-cell/in-vivo variants.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs, statistics, or trial data; References section citations unchanged and correctly attributed.

practice_boundaries.detail: Scope remains entirely experimental/technical screen diagnostics; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about human subjects.

methodological_ground.detail: Pre-fix FAIL trigger (Step 3's 'Replicate Pearson' formula conflating replicate and non-replicate pairs) is verified fixed by direct re-execution: the new condition-grouping code gives 0.7886812496284182 on real HAP1 TKOv3 data vs. the old naive formula's 0.6769896801914643 -- both values match the fix log exactly. No new methodological fallacy found; the MLE permutation-round gap (Input 6) is a reliability/documentation-completeness gap, not a fallacy in what is stated.

code_usability.detail: Every code block executed successfully on real or realistic data: Step 3 QC (fixed formula), Step 6a MAGeCK RRA (both label schemes), Step 6a BAGEL2 fc/bf with -s 42 (run twice, byte-identical), Step 6c drugZ, Step 6d/6e JACKS/Chronos API surface, Step 6b MAGeCK MLE (default and --permutation-round 10), Step 7 tier-consensus, and examples/crispr_pipeline.sh's flags all verified present in the installed MAGeCK 0.5.9.5.

functional_suitability.note: Both correctness defects found pre-fix (Replicate Pearson conflation; Step 2/Step 6a non-composing examples) are fixed and verified by direct re-execution. Remaining gap: Step 6b's MAGeCK MLE example doesn't carry forward sibling mageck-analysis's own fixed permutation-round reliability caveat.

reliability.note: Common Errors table now covers the BAGEL2 seed and the made-once-commitments risk with pointers to bagel-essentiality; still no row for MLE's default-permutation-round FDR instability, which this audit reproduced on real data (Input 6).

performance_context.note: Unchanged from pre-fix: token-efficient prose for the scope covered; code blocks remain concise, adapted patterns.

agent_usability.note: CN-threshold drift between SKILL.md and usage-guide.md is fixed and verified consistent; Step 0 made-once-commitments gate is now a numbered precondition in both documents. A separate, unfixed Replicate-Pearson threshold drift remains: Step 3's own 'Hard gates' line states >0.85 while the frontmatter, usage-guide.md, and the canonical sibling screen-qc all state a >=0.8 floor with 0.85 as the 'acceptable' (not fail) band.

human_usability.note: Forgiveness improved: the new Step 0 gives explicit recovery guidance (ask the user) for the made-once-commitments risk that pre-fix had only narrative treatment for.

security.note: Unchanged: no credential exposure, destructive operations, or prompt-injection vectors in any script or instruction.

maintainability.note: CN-bias threshold is now stated identically in both documents. The Replicate-Pearson threshold wording still drifts internally within SKILL.md itself (frontmatter vs. Step 3 body) -- a residual documentation-sync defect of the same class as the one that was fixed this round.

agent_specific.note: Composability materially improved: Step 7's tier-consensus code ran unmodified against the new seeded BAGEL2 output, and Step 2's and Step 6a's worked examples now compose without manual correction (verified against the published HAP1 TKOv3 benchmark). A real escape hatch (Step 0) now exists for missing made-once commitments. Step 6b's MLE example is the one remaining composability/escape-hatch gap: no warning that its own literal invocation uses an unreliable default.

recommendations.title: Step 6b's MAGeCK MLE example doesn't carry forward mageck-analysis's own fixed permutation-round caveat
recommendations.problem: Step 6b's mageck mle command sets no --permutation-round, silently using MAGeCK's noisy default of 2. On a 1,500-gene real-data subsample this flips 4/1500 genes' FDR<0.05 status against --permutation-round 10; sibling mageck-analysis's own audit found the same defect flips 40% of hits at full genome scale and now documents '>=10 for any FDR call near 0.05', but this pipeline's Step 6b and Related Skills sections never surface that caveat.
recommendations.root_cause: Step 6b's example was written before mageck-analysis's permutation-round finding existed, and this fix round's Related Skills cross-references were not revisited for it.
recommendations.fix: Add --permutation-round 10 (or an explicit caveat with a pointer to [[mageck-analysis]]'s permutation-round section) to Step 6b's mageck mle example, matching what bagel-essentiality's -s 42 seed and hit-calling's own cross-references already do for the BAGEL2 determinism fix in this same pipeline.

recommendations.title: Replicate Pearson threshold still drifts internally within SKILL.md itself
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's frontmatter states 'Replicate Pearson on log-counts >=0.8 (MAGeCK-VISPR floor; >0.85 acceptable, >0.95 ideal)', matching usage-guide.md and the canonical sibling screen-qc, but Step 3's own 'Hard gates from [[screen-qc]]' line states flatly 'Replicate Pearson on log-counts >0.85' -- using the 'acceptable' band as if it were the fail floor. This is the same class of documentation-sync defect as the CN-bias threshold that was fixed this round, just not caught by that fix.
recommendations.root_cause: The CN-threshold fix reconciled SKILL.md against usage-guide.md but did not audit SKILL.md's own two internal statements of the Replicate Pearson gate against each other or against screen-qc's canonical wording.
recommendations.fix: Make Step 3's 'Hard gates' line read '>=0.8 (MAGeCK-VISPR floor); >0.85 acceptable' verbatim, matching the frontmatter, usage-guide.md, and screen-qc.

recommendations.title: examples/crispr_pipeline.sh is not referenced from SKILL.md or usage-guide.md
recommendations.problem: The bundled examples/crispr_pipeline.sh (a complete, independently-runnable mageck count -> mageck test -> hit extraction script, verified to use only flags present in the installed MAGeCK 0.5.9.5) is never mentioned in either shipped document, so an agent following SKILL.md/usage-guide.md alone would not discover it.
recommendations.root_cause: The examples/ file was added without a cross-reference from the main documents.
recommendations.fix: Add one line in SKILL.md's Output Files or Related Skills section pointing to examples/crispr_pipeline.sh as a ready-to-run reference script.
